know_secure_design_justification: The primary developer knows secure design principles (least privilege, fail-safe defaults, input validation, minimal attack surface) and applies them; the security policy and enforced repository checks document this. know_common_errors_justification: The primary developer knows the common vulnerability classes for this kind of software (OWASP Top 10, CWE Top 25) and the methods to counter them; static analysis and dependency scanning run on every change. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/SECURITY.md
crypto_published_justification: All cryptographic operations (including PKCE code challenge generation with SHA-256 and TLS transport via Go standard library) rely exclusively on publicly published and reviewed algorithms. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/metadata/anime/mal/mal.go#L357-L365 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/SECURITY.md#L40
crypto_call_justification: The project does not implement custom cryptographic algorithms, delegating all cryptographic operations to Go standard library packages (crypto/rand, crypto/sha256, crypto/tls). Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/metadata/anime/mal/mal.go#L5-L6 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/docs/principles.md#L88-L91 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/SECURITY.md#L37-L44
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptographic functionality is provided exclusively by the Go standard library, which is free and open-source software under a BSD-3-Clause license. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/metadata/anime/mal/mal.go#L5-L6 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/SECURITY.md#L37 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/README.md#L35-L36
crypto_keylength_justification: Cryptographic defaults meet modern guidelines, using a 64-byte (512-bit) cryptographically random verifier and SHA-256 for PKCE, while TLS transport defaults to Go standard library cipher suites. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/metadata/anime/mal/mal.go#L356-L365 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/SECURITY.md#L40
crypto_working_justification: goenvoy implements no cryptography; TLS comes from Go crypto/tls and PKCE uses SHA-256. The one broken algorithm is MD5 in the Navidrome client, which the Subsonic token authentication protocol mandates (t = md5(password + salt)); the package documentation states the risk (token replay, offline password attack) and the mitigations (https baseURL, a password not shared with other services). Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/mediaserver/navidrome/navidrome.go#L59-L67 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/mediaserver/navidrome/navidrome.go#L98-L99 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/mediaserver/navidrome/AGENTS.md#L13-L17 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/metadata/anime/mal/mal.go#L356-L365
crypto_weaknesses_justification: PKCE in the MAL client uses SHA-256 over 64 random bytes; no SHA-1 or CBC mode in SSH is used. MD5 appears only where the Subsonic protocol mandates it, with the risk documented on navidrome.New. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/metadata/anime/mal/mal.go#L356-L365 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/mediaserver/navidrome/navidrome.go#L59-L67
crypto_pfs_justification: As a client library collection, goenvoy does not implement network key agreement protocols directly, delegating transport-level key exchange and perfect forward secrecy to the underlying Go standard library crypto/tls implementation. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/docs/principles.md#L90 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/SECURITY.md#L40
crypto_password_storage_justification: As a collection of client libraries, goenvoy does not store user passwords or authenticate inbound users; credentials exist solely in client memory structs during API execution and are never persisted to disk or databases. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/SECURITY.md#L39 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/docs/principles.md#L89
crypto_random_justification: The PKCE code verifier (MAL) and the Subsonic auth salt (Navidrome) come from crypto/rand. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/metadata/anime/mal/mal.go#L356-L365 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/mediaserver/navidrome/navidrome.go#L93-L97
delivery_mitm_justification: Software distribution and module retrieval use HTTPS exclusively via GitHub and standard Go module proxy endpoints (proxy.golang.org) to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/README.md#L63-L76 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/SECURITY.md#L15-L33
delivery_unsigned_justification: The project retrieves dependencies over HTTPS with cryptographic checksum verification enforced by go.sum, while all release archives are accompanied by cosign keyless signatures and SLSA-L3 provenance attestations. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/SECURITY.md#L15-L34 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml#L104-L133
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No vulnerability with a public disclosure older than 60 days is open: the repository has no security advisories and no open Dependabot alerts (GitHub API, checked 2026-10-25); govulncheck runs per module in CI and the last standard-library findings were fixed by raising the Go floor. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/Makefile#L65-L69 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L209-L236 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#L11
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been reported or found (no security advisories, no open Dependabot or critical code-scanning alerts, GitHub API checked 2026-10-25); reports are acknowledged within 72 hours with a remediation plan within 7 days. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/SECURITY.md#L3-L9
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The required CI check Secret scan (gitleaks) scans every commit in the history, not only the tip, and fails on any finding; local credential files are ignored by version control and tests use httptest with fake keys only. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L104-L125 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/.gitleaks.toml https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/.gitignore
static_analysis_justification: Static analysis is performed automatically in CI using gosec, Semgrep (with security-audit and golang rule packs), golangci-lint, and govulncheck on every proposed pull request and push. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L209-L236 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/.github/workflows/security-scan.yml#L23-L65 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/.golangci.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: Static analysis suites (gosec and Semgrep) specifically scan for common language and web security vulnerabilities, including credential leaks, path traversal, TLS bypasses, and weak cryptography. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/SECURITY.md#L52-L61 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/.github/workflows/security-scan.yml#L45-L50 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/.golangci.yml#L40-L43
static_analysis_fixed_justification: All findings from static analysis tools must be fixed prior to merge; CI gates enforce zero warnings from golangci-lint, zero gosec findings, and clean govulncheck reports. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#L41-L50 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/docs/principles.md#L22 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/.golangci.yml
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs automatically in CI on every push and pull request to the main branch via GitHub Actions workflows. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L12-L16 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/.github/workflows/security-scan.yml#L6-L10
dynamic_analysis_justification: Dynamic analysis is performed across all modules using Go's built-in race detector (go test -race -count=1), code coverage instrumentation, httptest HTTP integration tests, and Go fuzz tests (testing.F). Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/Makefile#L13-L17 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L209-L236 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/arr/client_test.go#L488-L497
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The software is written entirely in Go, a memory-safe language, and contains no C/C++ or unsafe Go code. Evidence: https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/docs/principles.md#L21 https://github.com/golusoris/goenvoy/blob/main/README.md#L45
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Dynamic analysis and test execution run with assertions enabled, including the Go runtime race detector (-race), boundary checks in constructors, and table-driven assertions with t.Errorf and t.Fatalf.
